summary: Proves a nilpotent-data obstruction and a non-equidimensional top-degree degeneracy, and gives an exact diagnostic showing that positivity and continuity alone do not imply locality.
detailedSummary: Identical reduced boundary/gauge data can have unreduced multiplicity one or two, requiring extra nilpotent length data. A dimension-two surface/curve fibre product has a nonzero curve-only bounded geometric input with zero degree-two moment measure. A two-point positive additive continuous map fails locality, but is not the actual kernel and does not disprove P12.4. Finite exact diagnostics passed on their expressly bounded domains.
text:
These examples distinguish genuine obstructions from missing proofs. They do not establish impossibility of reduced higher-dimensional P12.4.

For nilpotents, take R_1=k[[t]] and R_2=k[[t]][epsilon]/(epsilon^2). Both are excellent local rings and (t) is primary in both. Their reduced gauges and centred semivaluation boundaries are identical, because nilpotents have infinite value. Nevertheless length_(R_1)(R_1/(t^N))=N and length_(R_2)(R_2/(t^N))=2N. The bases are respectively t^i and t^i,epsilon t^i, 0≤i<N. Their multiplicities are one and two. Thus an assignment depending only on G331's reduced boundary and reduced gauge cannot recover both unreduced intersection multiplicities. Extra generic-length data are necessary for that different target. This is not an obstruction to the explicitly reduced construction.

For the non-equidimensional convention, let R=k[[x,y,z]]/(xy,xz), isomorphic to k[[y,z]] fibre-product over k with k[[x]]. Restriction to the two components gives pairs with equal constant terms; its kernel is (x) intersection (y,z)=(xy,xz). The ring is reduced, excellent and complete, of dimension two. Its normalization is S=k[[y,z]]×k[[x]], finite with quotient S/R one copy of k. Its conductor is the pair of maximal ideals, corresponding downstairs to m=(x,y,z). Every centred boundary point has finite conductor value. Thus the full boundary is the disjoint union of the full surface boundary and the curve point, with singleton fibres and clopen pieces.

Use gauge m and I_N=(y,z,x^N). This is primary. The rational profile u_N=−v(I_N)/N is identically −1/N on the surface boundary and −1 at the curve point. It converges uniformly to a C function u that is zero on the surface and −1 on the curve. This uses uniform closure, not an assumed increasing D closure. Equation (4) gives e_R(I_N,m)=1: the surface restriction is its maximal ideal in both slots, whose degree-two multiplicity is one, while the curve contributes no degree-two coefficient. The surface calculation follows from length(k[[y,z]]/(y,z)^t)=t(t+1)/2. Hence nu_m(u_N) has mass 1/N, and positivity makes its weak limit zero. N3 therefore gives nu_m(u)=0 although u is nonzero. The lower-dimensional point remains in the boundary and function class; it has zero top-degree contribution rather than an invented vertical degree. A curve product there would require the separate zero-potential convention.

For the locality diagnostic, take the compact discrete two-point space K={x,y}, its cone of all finite nonpositive functions, and F(u)=(−u(x)−u(y)) delta_x. This map is positive, additive, nonnegative-real homogeneous, uniformly continuous and continuous for bounded decreasing nets. But u=(−1,−1) and w=(−1,−2) agree on the open set U={x}, whereas F(u)|_U=2 delta_x and F(w)|_U=3 delta_x. Thus those formal properties alone do not imply locality. This map is not asserted to satisfy the primary mixed-multiplicity kernel or to disprove locality of n3's actual moment construction. A separate geometric proof remains necessary.

The fresh program exact_diagnostics.py enumerates finite basis counts and primary-gauge arithmetic from bounded-evidence-input.json, without importing or executing supplied programs. Its observed output was PASS on 48 residue-degree basis cases (d=2,3; r=1,2,3; N=1,...,8), eight nilpotent basis cases (N=1,...,8), and 27 two-branch gauge/test combinations using exact fractions. It checks the basis slopes and the identity that old branch mass a_q multiplied by b_q/a_q becomes b_q and gives unchanged homogeneous test moments. This is exhaustive only on those declared finite arithmetic inputs. It neither proves arbitrary-real coverage nor geometric locality or higher-dimensional Cartier comparison.

Artifacts: n6.md, bounded-evidence-input.json, exact_diagnostics.py and reports/exact-diagnostics.json. Rerun: python exact_diagnostics.py; python build_delivery.py.
